fullTextEN: Hello!
Do you like eating noodles?
In English, it's 'noodle',

fullTextZH: 可是在中文，我们一般有“面”还有“粉”。
fullTextEN: But in Chinese, we generally have 'mian' and 'fen'.

fullTextZH: 今天，我们一起去中国旅游！
fullTextEN: Today, we are going to travel to China together!
We will travel,
while eating noodles.
First, we are going to Xinjiang.

fullTextZH: 在新疆，最有名的一道菜是大盘鸡，
fullTextEN: In Xinjiang, the most famous dish is 'big plate chicken',
which is a very large plate of chicken,
with potatoes inside,
with chicken and also noodles.

fullTextZH: 所以，面条吸收了很多味道，
fullTextEN: So, the noodles absorb a lot of flavors,
so it's very delicious.
I recommend it to you!

fullTextZH: 现在，我们从新疆去四川。
fullTextEN: Now, we are going from Xinjiang to Sichuan.

fullTextZH: 在四川，有一种面很有意思，
fullTextEN: In Sichuan, there is a kind of noodle that is very interesting,
It's called 'ranmian'.
Why is it called 'ranmian'?

fullTextZH: 因为以前，燃面很油、很油，
fullTextEN: Because in the past, 'ranmian' was very oily, very oily,

fullTextZH: 所以，如果你点火，真的可以烧起来。
fullTextEN: So, if you light it, it can really catch fire.
So, it's called 'burning noodles'.

fullTextZH: 我第一次吃，不是在四川，
fullTextEN: The first time I ate it was not in Sichuan,
I was in Beijing.
The first time eating burning noodles,
I was amazed,
I thought it was very delicious.

fullTextZH: 所以，我也推荐燃面给你们吃。
fullTextEN: So, I also recommend burning noodles to you all.
Now, we go to
Guizhou.
I have never been to Guizhou,

fullTextZH: 可是，我听过贵州有一个面，叫肠旺面。
fullTextEN: but I heard Guizhou has a noodle called 'Changwang Noodles'.
'Chang' is pig's large intestine,
'Wang' is pig's blood.

fullTextZH: 对，中国人很喜欢吃动物内脏，
fullTextEN: Yes, Chinese people really like to eat animal organs,

fullTextZH: 可能很多人觉得很可怕，
fullTextEN: Maybe many people find it scary,

fullTextZH: 可是，我觉得动物内脏的口感非常特别，
fullTextEN: but I think the texture of animal organs is very special,
I really like it.

fullTextZH: 所以，我没有吃过肠旺面，
fullTextEN: So, I have never eaten Changwang Noodles,
but I want to try.
Now, we go.
Yunnan.

fullTextZH: 在云南，最有名的米线叫过桥米线。
fullTextEN: In Yunnan, the most famous rice noodles are called 'Crossing the Bridge Noodles'.
If you eat 'Crossing the Bridge Noodles',
they will give you a bowl of soup.
This bowl of soup doesn't look hot,
but actually, it's very hot, very hot,

fullTextZH: 因为这碗汤里有很多、很多鸡油，
fullTextEN: because this bowl of soup has a lot, a lot of chicken oil,
so it's very, very hot.
So, they give you a bowl of soup,

fullTextZH: 然后，他们给你很多、很多料，
fullTextEN: then, they give you a lot, a lot of ingredients,
for example, pork,
for example, fish,
for example, vegetables,
and quail eggs.
So, you put the pork,
put the fish, put the quail eggs,
put the vegetables in,
then wait.

fullTextZH: 等一会儿，然后，你就可以吃这个过桥米线。
fullTextEN: Wait a while, then you can eat these 'Crossing the Bridge Noodles'.

fullTextZH: 我非常、非常喜欢，因为过桥米线有很多、很多料，
fullTextEN: I really, really like it because crossing-the-bridge rice noodles have a lot, a lot of ingredients.
So, I recommend it for you to eat.
Now, we go to
Guangxi.

fullTextZH: 在广西，最有名的粉丝叫螺蛳粉。
fullTextEN: In Guangxi, the most famous noodles are called snail noodles.
These noodles are very interesting,

fullTextZH: 因为它的汤是螺蛳和别的东西做的。
fullTextEN: because their soup is made from snails and other things.

fullTextZH: 螺蛳粉里有很多、很多料，
fullTextEN: Snail noodles have a lot, a lot of ingredients,

fullTextZH: 可是，有一个料很特别，就是酸笋。
fullTextEN: but there is one very special ingredient, which is pickled bamboo shoots.

fullTextZH: 这个酸笋，因为它发酵过，
fullTextEN: These pickled bamboo shoots, because they are fermented,
so, some people think they smell bad.

fullTextZH: 所以，有的人不喜欢吃螺蛳粉，
fullTextEN: So, some people don't like to eat snail noodles,
they think snail noodles have
a very smelly taste.

fullTextZH: 可是，我非常喜欢吃螺蛳粉。
fullTextEN: But, I really like to eat snail noodles.

fullTextZH: 现在，你可以在亚洲超市买到螺蛳粉，
fullTextEN: Now, you can buy snail noodles at Asian supermarkets,
also very delicious.
If you are not afraid of
the smelly taste,
you can try it.
Now, we go
to Guangdong.

fullTextZH: 在广东，最有名的粉叫肠粉。
fullTextEN: In Guangdong, the most famous noodle is called cheung fun.
Don't worry, it's not pig intestines,
it's a type of noodle,

fullTextZH: 可是，它看起来像猪大肠，
fullTextEN: but it looks like pig intestines,
but without pig intestines.
I have a friend from Beijing,
he went to Guangdong.
During breakfast,
his Guangdong friend asked him:
"What do you want to eat?
How about eating cheung fun?"

fullTextZH: 我的北京朋友觉得：“什么肠粉？
fullTextEN: My Beijing friend thought: "What cheung fun?
Why eat pig intestines in the morning?"
Then, he realized: "Oh,

fullTextZH: 肠粉和猪大肠没有关系。”
fullTextEN: cheung fun has nothing to do with pig intestines."
Guangdong people often eat
cheung fun for breakfast.
Cheung fun usually contains pork,
Beef, and also shrimp.
You can go to 'yumcha' to try rice noodle rolls.
Now, we go
Fujian.

fullTextZH: 在福建，有一种面很特别，
fullTextEN: In Fujian, there is a type of noodle that is very special,
called Mianxian paste.

fullTextZH: 他们用很细、很细的面做的面线糊，
fullTextEN: They use very thin, very thin noodles to make Mianxian paste,

fullTextZH: 所以看起来是宝宝吃的东西。
fullTextEN: so it looks like something for babies to eat.

fullTextZH: 其实，面线糊里有很多、很多料，
fullTextEN: Actually, there are many, many ingredients in Mianxian paste,
so at first I didn't like it,

fullTextZH: 可是慢慢地，我越来越喜欢。
fullTextEN: but gradually, I liked it more and more.
Now, we go
Shaanxi.

fullTextZH: 陕西人非常、非常喜欢吃面，
fullTextEN: Shaanxi people really, really like to eat noodles,
but there is a type of noodle that is very famous,
its name is Biangbiang noodles.
This noodle is very famous,

fullTextZH: 因为“biang”这个字看起来太难、太难。
fullTextEN: because the character 'biang' looks too difficult, too difficult.

fullTextZH: 其实，它不是一个真的汉字，
fullTextEN: Actually, it is not a real Chinese character,

fullTextZH: 它是很多、很多汉字放在一起。
fullTextEN: it is many, many Chinese characters put together.
So, if you type,
You cannot type the character 'biang'.
Why is it called biangbiang noodles?

fullTextZH: 因为你做这个面，它会有“biangbiang”的声音，
fullTextEN: Because when you make these noodles, they make a 'biangbiang' sound,
So, they are called biangbiang noodles.
Now, we go to
Shanxi.

fullTextZH: 在山西，有一种面很有名，
fullTextEN: In Shanxi, there is a type of noodle that is very famous,
called
knife-cut noodles.
It's when they take a dough,
then take a knife,
and cut the noodles.

fullTextZH: 大部分的面是拉的，对不对？
fullTextEN: Most noodles are pulled, right?
But knife-cut noodles are not pulled,
they are cut.
So they are very famous,

fullTextZH: 因为他的做法有一点点不一样。
fullTextEN: because their method is a little different.

fullTextZH: 好，中国还有很多、很多面的种类。
fullTextEN: Well, China also has many, many types of noodles.

fullTextZH: 我还说了福建的面线糊，

Then, I mentioned Shaanxi's biangbiang noodles,

fullTextZH: 然后，我说了山西的刀削面。

fullTextEN: China has very, very many types of noodles,

fullTextZH: 每一个地方都吃不太一样的面。
fullTextEN: Every place eats slightly different noodles.
So, if you like eating noodles,

fullTextZH: 你一定要去中国，一边旅游，一边吃面！
fullTextEN: You must go to China, travel and eat noodles!
